payload.title: Four workspace-nested entries of the root package-lock.json (the TypeScript compilers of libs/farm-shared, libs/node-components and mcp/farm-management, and @types/eslint of tools/eslint-rules; all dev) carried a version but neither resolved nor integrity, so npm ci installed them with no hash to check; every other registry entry carries both
evidence: package-lock.json:216 (libs/farm-shared/node_modules/typescript 5.3.3 at origin/main 645c5313: no resolved, no integrity, dev)
package-lock.json:260 (libs/node-components/node_modules/typescript 5.3.3 at origin/main 645c5313: no resolved, no integrity, dev)
package-lock.json:312 (mcp/farm-management/node_modules/typescript 5.4.5 at origin/main 645c5313: no resolved, no integrity, dev)
package-lock.json:41438 (tools/eslint-rules/node_modules/@types/eslint 8.56.12 at origin/main 645c5313: no resolved, no integrity, dev)
payload.rule_violated: Every registry entry of a committed npm lockfile carries resolved and integrity, so npm ci verifies every tarball it installs
payload.notes: Found by the Snowball pilot's dependency and profile checks. 4 of the 49 workspace-nested registry entries lacked both fields; none of the 2891 hoisted entries lacked either. npm 10.9.9 npm install --package-lock-only neither restores nor strips the fields, and no check in the repository requires them. LOW: all four are dev tooling, and each registry dist.integrity equals the sha512 of the downloaded tarball, so the gap is a missing check with no sign that any tarball differed. Fix: the four entries carry the registry's resolved and integrity. A guard that keeps both fields on every lock entry is an operator decision outside this change.
